author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Fifty-four members of the New Hampshire Army National Guard are preparing to deploy to Texas next month for a year-long mission supporting U.S. Customs and Border Protection, New Hampshire Public Radio reported Monday.
A departure ceremony was held Saturday in Concord. The soldiers are expected to support aerial and ground reconnaissance along the U.S.-Mexico border as part of an ongoing federal security operation.

The deployment will include 14 soldiers from a Lakota helicopter unit based in Concord and 40 members of the 262nd Engineer Construction Company based in Rochester. The Guard said the units will assist the federal border mission rather than operate as a separate state deployment.

It will be the third time in six years that New Hampshire’s Army National Guard has supported a border mission. In 2021, 215 members took part in year-long deployments; in 2024, 15 soldiers were sent for 60 days to support a Texas state border mission.

The New Hampshire Guard said more than 2,100 National Guard members from more than 20 states are currently deployed in support of federal security operations at the border. The latest New Hampshire units are expected to mobilize in October.
dek: Two New Hampshire Army National Guard units are expected to deploy next month for a year-long mission supporting U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
headline: 54 New Hampshire National Guard members prepare for Texas border mission
